$$

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =11 \\  & =-3\,311-(-3\,322) \\  & =-3\,300-(-3\,311) \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

The $n$th term of our arithmetic sequence, denoted ${a}_{n},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =-3\,322\,+(n-1)\cdot 11 \\  & =-3\,322+11n-11 \\  & =11n-3\,333.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can express $A$ in set-builder notation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={11n-3\,333:n\in N,\,1\le n\le N}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}11N-3\,333 & =2\,332 \\ 11N & =5\,665 \\ N & =\frac{5\,665}{11} \\ N & =515\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =10+(n-1)\cdot 9 \\  & =10+9n-9 \\  & =9n+1.\end{aligned}

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}9N+1 & =865 \\ 9N & =864 \\ N & =\frac{864}{9} \\ N & =96\end{aligned}

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
5, \quad 6, \quad 7, \quad 8, \quad 9
$$

$$
\emptyset = \{\}
$$

has cardinality $\left|\emptyset\right| = 0$ since it contains no elements. The empty set is the *only* set with cardinality zero.

$$
|\mathbb N| = |\{1,2,3,\ldots\}| = \,?
$$
